body:
## Which Ninja Slushi should you buy?

Every Slushi works the same way: pour in a cold drink, choose a programme, and a chilled, stirring vessel turns it to slush in roughly half an hour to an hour. You pull a lever to dispense. The differences are capacity, number of programmes and whether you can make two drinks at once. These are the main UK models, with specs from Ninja and the retailers:

- **Slushi FS301UK (original):** 2.5L vessel (1.9L maximum fill), about seven servings, five presets: slush, frozen cocktail, frappé, milkshake and frozen juice. Ninja says drinks can be ready in as little as 30 minutes. **Best for most households.**
- **Slushi with SlushAssist FS351UK:** the newer version of the original, with the same seven-serving size but sensing technology that adjusts the freeze to what's in the vessel. Ninja lists it at £309.99 with no discount yet, so the FS301UK is better value for now.
- **Slushi XL FS601UK:** a 3.7L vessel for up to ten drinks and six one-touch programmes. Worth it if you host often.
- **Slushi Max FS605UK:** up to 12 drinks per batch and six programmes, including a stronger frozen cocktail setting. A party machine.
- **Slushi Twist FS701UK/FS702UK:** two separate vessels, so you can make two different drinks at once, such as a kids' slush and an adult cocktail. The FS701 has fixed slanted spouts; the FS702 has swappable spouts.

For a family of four who'll mostly make fruit slushies and the odd milkshake, the original FS301UK is plenty. It's also the cheapest by a long way: £249 at John Lewis today against £309.99 for the Twist at Ninja and £349.99 for the Max at Argos.

## Good prices to aim for

- **Slushi FS301UK:** £249 is a fair price, but Ninja had it at £199.99 in late October and price trackers have seen it slightly lower over the past three months. **Under £210 is a great price.**
- **Slushi Twist FS701UK:** £309.99 is £100 off the £409.99 list price. A good price for a two-vessel machine.
- **Slushi Max:** Argos had it at £259.99 on 12 November; two days later it was back to £349.99. **Wait for £260 or less**, which is likely again in Black Friday week.
- **Slushi XL:** Ninja is running Black Friday prices on frozen treats, but we couldn't confirm the XL's price today. Aim for under £270.

Ninja's site also has a 10% off code, BLACKFRIDAY, on selected items until the end of Monday 16 November. Check whether your model is included at the basket.

## When do Ninja Slushi prices drop?

Ninja discounts heavily through November, and prices have already moved several times this month. Black Friday itself is on 27 November 2026. Retailers price-match each other quickly, so a drop at Ninja or Amazon usually shows up at John Lewis, Argos and AO within a day or two. If you want one by Christmas, buying in Black Friday week gives you the best price and plenty of time for delivery.

## What to know before you buy

**It needs counter space.** The Slushi is a tall, heavy appliance that's best left in one place rather than pulled out of a cupboard each time.

**Drinks need sugar.** Ninja advises that drinks need some sugar content to slush properly. Diet and zero-sugar drinks tend to come out icy or not freeze at all, so check the manual's guidance if you want low-sugar slush.

**It's not a blender.** It won't crush ice or blend fruit. Blend first, then pour the juice in.

**Batch size is the real choice.** A seven-serving machine is plenty for a family. Only buy the XL, Max or Twist if you regularly make drinks for a crowd or want two flavours at once.

For more Ninja kitchen deals, see our [Ninja Black Friday deals guide](/guides/ninja-black-friday-deals-2026/) and [Ninja Creami deals](/guides/ninja-creami-deals-uk/), or browse [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/).

### Which Ninja Slushi is best?

The original FS301UK is the best value for most people. Choose the Twist if you want two different drinks at once, or the Max or XL for large batches.

### How long does a Ninja Slushi take?

Ninja says as little as 30 minutes for the original, depending on how cold the drink is when it goes in. Starting with chilled liquid makes it quicker.

### Can you make alcoholic slushies in a Ninja Slushi?

Yes. There's a frozen cocktail preset on every model. Too much alcohol stops the drink freezing, so follow Ninja's recipes for the right ratio.

### Is the Ninja Slushi worth it?

If you'd make slush or frozen drinks most weeks in summer and at parties, yes. If it would be used a few times a year, it's a lot of money and counter space, so wait for Black Friday prices.

### Will the Ninja Slushi be cheaper on Black Friday?

Probably. The original was £199.99 at Ninja in October and the Max was £259.99 at Argos earlier this week, so both have already been lower than today's prices.
